task.description:
DESIGN AMENDMENT (a real gap in the original approved design, found live by TEST-DESIGNER's own mix letflow.check.test run, not covered by any of the original design's OQ-1..OQ-6). Read handoffs/WF02-REQ372-20260921/step-03-test-designer.json in full for the exact evidence: mix letflow.check.test on this branch now shows combined 4522 tests, 32 failures (4496/4528 passed), and 31 of the 32 share one root cause -- Letflow.Definitions.SemanticValidation.field_existence_violations/3 (lib/letflow/definitions/semantic_validation.ex, around line 300-306) flags EVERY {:var, path} reference in a gateway condition as an undeclared-variable violation whenever `declared_fields` (the VariableSchema fetch result) is an EMPTY map -- because Map.has_key?/2 against an empty map is always false. Since VariableSchema registration is optional today and most pre-existing process-definition fixtures across the suite (req207_vortex_test.exs, req208_meridian_test.exs, req206_swiftroute_test.exs, scheduler_req188_test.exs, engine_test.exs, and more) never registered a VariableSchema at all, activate/2's new hard gate now blocks activation for essentially every pre-existing definition that has zero declared fields -- treating 'no schema was ever declared for this process' as 'every referenced field is a typo', which is not the intent of this requirement (REQ-372's own scope is catching a genuinely mis-typed/mis-typed-against reference against a schema the author DID declare, not retroactively demanding every pre-existing process backfill a full VariableSchema before it can activate).

Produce a narrow AMENDMENT to lib/letflow/design/req372-semantic-decision-rule-validation.md (edit the existing file in place -- add a new subsection under an appropriate existing section, e.g. after S2's type-pair table or as a new S2.x, clearly marked as an amendment with today's date and the reason) deciding and recording explicitly: when the definition's VariableSchema fetch returns EMPTY (zero declared fields registered for this process at all), does Letflow.Definitions.SemanticValidation.validate/2 (a) skip both violation classes entirely for that definition (return {valid: true, violations: []} unconditionally, since there is no schema to check against), or (b) some other explicit, justified behavior? State your decision and reasoning explicitly -- this is exactly the kind of boundary this requirement's own acceptance criteria (AC3, 'the comparable/non-comparable type-pair table is stated explicitly ... not left implicit') demands be recorded, not left implicit, and it directly determines whether hundreds of pre-existing fixtures keep working. Also state explicitly: does this change interact with or weaken any of the 10 original acceptance criteria (it should not -- AC1-AC6 all describe definitions that DO have a VariableSchema with real declared fields, so exempting the zero-schema case should be fully compatible) -- confirm this in writing. Update the @spec-style description for Letflow.Definitions.SemanticValidation.validate/2 (and field_existence_violations/3 if its signature/behavior changes) to reflect the amendment. This is a signature/behavior-shape amendment only -- no literal Elixir code bodies (same no-implementation-code rule as the original design gate).

You are on branch feature/WF02-REQ372-20260921 -- verify with git branch --show-current, pull if needed.

REWORK ITERATION 1: CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (step-03d) FAILed this amendment on exactly one point -- your own §2.5.4 claim that 'AC1-AC6 test cases never reach the new empty-declared_fields branch' is FALSE. The gate independently found three already-committed TEST-DESIGNER test cases that deliberately construct an EMPTY declared_fields map and assert a violation IS produced -- behavior your amendment's guard now silently suppresses: (1) test/letflow/definitions/semantic_validation_test.exs:106-113 (calls validate(graph, %{}), expects one violation message); (2) test/letflow/definitions/semantic_validation_activation_test.exs:211-231 (the AC6 'reverse' test -- expects valid: false with variable_schemas rows removed); (3) semantic_validation_activation_test.exs:241-259 (same pattern via validate_definition_graph/2 directly). Everything else about the amendment (the skip-when-empty decision itself, its reasoning, the guard's placement, no-implementation-code) was independently verified sound and is NOT in question here -- do not redesign the exemption mechanism. Fix, narrowly: revise §2.5.4 to honestly acknowledge these three existing tests test behavior that directly contradicts the now-decided semantics (an empty declared_fields map means 'no schema was ever declared, skip validation entirely' -- consistently, regardless of whether the process previously had a non-empty schema that was later cleared to empty, since validate/2 cannot distinguish 'never had one' from 'had one, now cleared' by construction, and the design's whole point is not to special-case that). State explicitly, with reasoning, that these three test scenarios must be REVISED by TEST-DESIGNER to match the amended semantics (not that the design should change to accommodate them) -- and be explicit about what the corrected expectation for each of the three should be (e.g. test 1 and test 3 should now expect valid: true/no violations for an empty schema; the AC6 'reverse' test's premise needs re-examination -- AC6 is about a fresh call reflecting CURRENT state, not about every state mutation necessarily producing a stricter verdict, and 'schema fully cleared' is itself a legitimate current state under the skip-when-empty policy). This is rework iteration 1 of max_rework 3. On completion, set this handoff's status to COMPLETED and result to a genuine first-hand PASS/FAIL report as normal.
acceptance_criteria: the empty-VariableSchema behavior is decided and stated explicitly, with reasoning
the amendment confirms (or corrects) compatibility with all 10 original acceptance criteria
no implementation code (function bodies) introduced -- signature/behavior description only

the fix, once implemented, must not require any of the ~31 pre-existing failing fixtures to be individually modified -- the amendment must work by construction, without editing unrelated test fixtures
the three test-conflict scenarios found by the amendment regate are explicitly acknowledged and their required revised expectations stated

result.summary: REWORK ITERATION 1 complete. Revised S2.5.4 only (S2.5.1-S2.5.3 and S2.5.5 untouched -- the skip-when-empty decision and its exemption mechanism are NOT changed) in lib/letflow/design/req372-semantic-decision-rule-validation.md to honestly acknowledge the three test conflicts CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's step-03d regate found, and added a new S2.5.4.1 stating the required TEST-DESIGNER revisions. Corrected the AC2 bullet: the AC's own proving example stays non-empty-declared_fields and compatible, but the adjacent test at semantic_validation_test.exs:106-113 (`validate(graph, %{})`, asserts one violation message) is now acknowledged as broken by this amendment and requiring revision. Corrected the AC6 bullet: retracted this section's own prior false claim that the committed 'reverse' AC6 test (semantic_validation_activation_test.exs:211-231) keeps declared_fields non-empty across both calls -- it does not, it starts with zero rows and asserts a violation on the first (empty) call, which this amendment's guard now overrides to valid:true/violations:[]. S2.5.4.1 states, with reasoning, that all three named tests (the two above plus semantic_validation_activation_test.exs:241-259) must be revised by TEST-DESIGNER, not that S2.5.1's decision should change: an empty declared_fields map means 'no schema was ever declared,' validate/2 cannot and should not distinguish that from 'had one, later cleared to zero rows' by construction. Corrected expectations stated per test: (1) semantic_validation_test.exs:106-113 should assert messages(result) == [] for the empty-schema call, since field_existence_violations/3 (and nearest_declared_field/2) is never invoked when declared_fields == %{} -- its original 'no suggestion clause' intent is moot for this specific case. (2) The AC6 reverse test's premise needs re-examination -- AC6 is about a fresh call reflecting CURRENT state, not about every mutation direction producing a stricter verdict, and 'schema empty' is itself a legitimate current state under skip-when-empty; recommended fix is a different before/after pair that never ends in an empty schema (seed 'customer_name' only first -- non-empty but still missing 'amount', a genuine S2.2 violation -- then seed 'amount' and assert success), with a weaker fallback of revising the first assertion in place to valid:true/violations:[] and dropping the undeclared_variable_reference check. (3) semantic_validation_activation_test.exs:241-259 should either assert the now-correct valid:true/violations:[] directly (weaker, loses its own test intent) or, preferred, seed a non-'amount' field first so the mismatch it demonstrates is a genuine S2.2 violation against a non-empty schema, preserving its 'reports without blocking draft save' intent. All three revisions are confined to the two REQ-372 test files TEST-DESIGNER owns; none touch semantic_validation.ex, definitions.ex, or any of the ~31 pre-existing fixtures.
